\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{وادی} (vādī)}{وادی (vādī)}]{\ur{وادی} (vādī) — a valley}

\label{lesson:UR-C190-vadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for right away, then the Urdu for late.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{وادی}}
\textbf{\ur{وادی}} — \emph{vādī} — \textquotedblleft{}a valley\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{وادی}} (\emph{vādī}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{wādī}, \textquotedblleft{}a valley, a river bed\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{w-d-y} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{چڑیا} \ur{گھر} (chiṛyā ghar)}{چڑیا گھر (chiṛyā ghar)}]{\ur{چڑیا} \ur{گھر} (chiṛyā ghar) — a zoo}

\label{lesson:UR-C190-chirya-ghar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for late, then the Urdu for a valley.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{چڑیا} \ur{گھر}}
\textbf{\ur{چڑیا} \ur{گھر}} — \emph{chiṛyā ghar} — \textquotedblleft{}a zoo\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{چڑیا} \ur{گھر}} (\emph{chiṛyā ghar}) is \textquotedblleft{}bird house\textquotedblright{}. \emph{chiṛyā}, \textquotedblleft{}bird\textquotedblright{}, comes from Sanskrit \emph{caṭaka}, \textquotedblleft{}sparrow\textquotedblright{}, through a variant \emph{*ciṭaka} (CDIAL 4571). \emph{ghar}, \textquotedblleft{}house\textquotedblright{}, is inherited; it is usually taken as a popular form of Sanskrit \emph{gṛha}, a link CDIAL calls phonetically difficult (CDIAL 4428).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for late, then the Urdu for a valley, then say \emph{chiṛyā ghar} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مکان} (makān)}{مکان (makān)}]{\ur{مکان} (makān) — a dwelling, a house}

\label{lesson:UR-C190-makan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a university, then the Urdu for a college.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مکان}}
\textbf{\ur{مکان}} — \emph{makān} — \textquotedblleft{}a dwelling, a house\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مکان}} (\emph{makān}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{makān}, \textquotedblleft{}a place\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{k-w-n} (Lane). Urdu uses it for a house.
\end{cousinweb}
